sections.label: Left eye
sections.description: Photoreceptors and lamina of the left eye. Lesioning blinds that eye.

sections.label: Right eye
sections.description: Photoreceptors and lamina of the right eye. Lesioning blinds that eye.

sections.label: Motion detectors (T4, T5)
sections.description: Direction-selective neurons that report which way edges move. T4 sees bright edges, T5 dark ones.

sections.label: Looming detectors (LPLC2, LC4, LPLC1, LPLC4)
sections.description: Respond to objects rapidly approaching, like a block flying at the fly. They drive escape behavior.

sections.label: Visual feature detectors (LC neurons)
sections.description: Lobula columnar neurons. Each type is tuned to a visual feature and sends it to the central brain.

sections.label: Wide-field motion cells (HS, VS)
sections.description: Large cells that sense the fly's own turning from whole-scene motion.

sections.label: Central brain relay
sections.description: Central neurons that carry signals from the visual detectors to the descending neurons in this model.

sections.label: Giant fiber (DNp01)
sections.description: The escape command neuron that triggers a takeoff jump.

sections.label: All descending neurons
sections.description: The brain's motor commands to the body. Silencing them stops every action.

sections.label: Octopamine neurons
sections.description: The fly's arousal system, roughly its fight-or-flight signal.

sections.label: Serotonin neurons
sections.description: Shape mood-like states such as aggression and quiescence.

moods.name: arousal
moods.label: Arousal
moods.description: Drives octopamine neurons, which turn up the gain of the circuits they reach.

moods.name: reward_drive
moods.label: Reward drive
moods.description: Drives dopamine neurons, which signal reward and motivation and raise their targets' gain.

moods.name: calm
moods.label: Calm
moods.description: Drives serotonin neurons. In this model serotonin turns gain down, a stand-in for quiescence.
